chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) about the night prayer and the witr prayer at the beginning of the night while traveling, if I feared the cold or if there was an ailment. He said, 'There is no harm; I do that.'
ai.seo_question: When can a traveler perform night prayer and witr if they fear cold or illness?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of night prayers during travel, specifically allowing the performance of *witr* and *salat al-layl* at the beginning of the night when cold or illness is feared. This ruling highlights the principle of *rukhas* (divine concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing ease and health preservation without invalidating the spiritual merit of the night worship. The Imam’s personal practice serves as a definitive precedent for combining these prayers early in the night under such conditions.
